collection: NERDC JSS 1 Physical and Health Education first aid and preparedness
note: Original classroom practice, including two supervised simulations. Independent academic review pending.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.learningObjective: Recognise when a hazard prevents safe approach.
questions.prompt: A pupil slips beside scattered glass in the school corridor. From a clear doorway, you can speak to the pupil. Which response is appropriate before approaching?
questions.answer: Stay clear of the glass, alert a teacher and keep others back from a safe position.
questions.explanation: Checking for hazards first helps protect the injured pupil and anyone who might help. A teacher can arrange a safe approach.
options: Step between the pieces of glass to reach the pupil.
Stay clear of the glass, alert a teacher and keep others back from a safe position.
Ask nearby pupils to gather close and watch.
Sweep the glass away with your bare hands.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.learningObjective: Communicate the location and observed facts when seeking first-aid help.
questions.prompt: In a teacher-led role-play, you see a pupil scrape an arm near the school court. The pupil is awake and can speak. Report the incident to the adult playing the school first aider. Include where the pupil is, what happened and what you observed.
questions.answer: For example, “Please come to the school court beside the gate. A pupil scraped an arm on the bench. They are awake and speaking.”
questions.explanation: A clear handover helps the first aider locate the person and decide what to check on arrival.

markingGuide.description: Makes a clear request for first-aid help.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.learningObjective: Explain how planning and rehearsal prepare people for an emergency.
questions.prompt: A school assigns staff to guide classes to an assembly point and rehearses the route on a normal school day. Explain why both actions are examples of preparedness.
questions.answer: The assignments tell staff who will guide each class. Rehearsing lets staff and pupils practise the route before they need it during an emergency.
questions.explanation: Preparedness builds the ability to respond through advance planning and practice.

markingGuide.description: Explains the value of assigning responsibilities.
Explains the value of rehearsing before an emergency.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.learningObjective: Use a known hazard to choose a route in a preparedness plan.
questions.prompt: A school has two marked paths to its assembly point. Heavy rain often floods the low path. The raised path stays clear and the school has approved it for use when the low path floods. Which choice should a flood drill practise?
questions.answer: Use the approved raised path and keep the group away from the flooded path.
questions.explanation: The route choice uses knowledge of where the hazard occurs and the school’s agreed alternative.
options: Cross the low path because it is shorter.
Gather beside the flooded path to check its depth.
Use the approved raised path and keep the group away from the flooded path.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.learningObjective: Demonstrate route selection and accountability in a tabletop exercise.
questions.prompt: In a teacher-led tabletop drill, the teacher supplies a school plan with two approved routes and an assembly point. One route is marked blocked. Use tokens to move a class along the clear route. At the assembly point, compare the tokens with the teacher’s class list and report any mismatch.
questions.answer: Move the class tokens together along the clear approved route. At the assembly point, check them against the class list and report any missing token to the teacher in charge.
questions.explanation: The simulation checks how pupils follow a plan and verify that everyone is accounted for.

markingGuide.description: Moves the group along the selected route.
Checks the tokens against the class list at the assembly point.
Reports the result of the check accurately.
